summary: Kokoro-82M v1.0 runs on the RTX 5080 (median RTF 0.011, 15/15 lines) and on 4 CPU threads (median RTF 0.142, 15/15 lines). Four cast voices are blends of 2-3 preset packs, saved as .npy and .json. The espeak fallback gives phonemes for all invented names tested. The English preset packs have no documented origin; the best male packs are only graded C+.

licences.first_line: license: apache-2.0 (card metadata; the repo has no LICENSE file; not gated; base_model yl4579/StyleTTS2-LJSpeech)
Only grades and hashes; no per-voice provenance or licence text for English packs. The card says training audio includes synthetic audio from closed TTS providers (their terms are not stated).

licences.what: espeak-ng (espeak-ng.dll and data bundled in espeakng-loader)
licences.first_line: GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 29 June 2007 (GPL-3.0)

installed.source: explosion GitHub release wheel (12.8 MB), installed from a local copy; misaki would otherwise run spacy.cli.download at first use

downloaded.note: config.json, kokoro-v1_0.pth, 28 English voice packs (af_, am_, bf_, bm_). Pickle .pth/.pt: the makers ship nothing else.

weightsLoading: kokoro/model.py line 68: torch.load(model, map_location='cpu', weights_only=True); kokoro/pipeline.py line 147: torch.load(f, weights_only=True). The adapter also wraps torch.load and refuses any call without weights_only=True, and loads the packs itself with weights_only=True. No trust_remote_code.

voices.note: Kokoro cannot build a voice from a description. The makers do not document the origin of the English preset packs, so a blend is artificial only in the sense that it is no single preset. No male pack is graded B- or better (best C+), so both male voices rest on C+/C packs. Female blends use only packs graded B- or better. Blends mix American and British packs and are spoken through the American G2P. The seed fixes only the decoder noise; the style tensors are deterministic.

timings.note: The timed span is the whole pipeline call (G2P with espeak fallback plus model), one chunk per line, so first audio equals total time (no streaming inside a chunk). G2P alone took about 2-4 ms per line (g2p_s in timing.json). The warm-up sentence was untimed.

sizes.note: .venv-voice/kokoro (torch cu128 dominates); HF cache 327 MB of model files plus 12.8 MB spaCy wheel; assets/audio/voice/kokoro about 25 MB of output

telemetry: A grep of kokoro, misaki and espeakng_loader found no analytics, telemetry, requests or urllib use. Only network use is huggingface_hub downloads of model, config and voices when no local path is given; huggingface_hub has its own telemetry switch, set off with HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1. Misaki G2P calls spacy.cli.download('en_core_web_sm') at construction if the model is missing (a run-time install from GitHub); avoided by installing the wheel beforehand. The adapter sets HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and passes local paths. Only spaCy .py files were grepped for telemetry (no hits); transformers was not searched.
problems: The adapter file is named kokoro.py like the package; the adapter folder is removed from sys.path at start so that import kokoro finds the package.
On Windows setting CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the empty string deletes the variable and left the card visible; the adapter uses -1 instead.
snapshot_download(local_files_only=True) calls the partial English snapshot incomplete; the adapter reads the pinned snapshot folder directly.
One tiny torch matmul check of the card (about a second) was made once without the lock, during installation.
The cuda and cpu runs waited for the lock behind other agents; timings were taken inside the lock.

Licence point for later: espeak-ng (GPL-3.0) and phonemizer-fork (GPLv3+) are needed for the out-of-dictionary fallback that the invented names require. Shipping or linking them needs a decision. Without the fallback misaki drops unknown words.

The weights licence rests on the card metadata tag; the HF repo has no LICENSE file. Training data includes synthetic audio from closed TTS providers whose terms are not stated; the base model is StyleTTS2-LJSpeech.
notVerified: How any voice sounds (nobody can hear)
Whether invented names are pronounced acceptably (only that phonemes are produced)
Whether the English packs have a real-person template
Word error rate and speaker consistency (score.py is separate)
